newsitem.title: UK: UK beet crop still on course after frost,dry spell.
newsitem.headline: UK beet crop still on course after frost,dry spell.

text.p: Britain's 1997/98 sugar beet crop appears to be back on course after the dry spells and frost experienced at the critical germination stage soon after planting, beet experts said on Monday.

Last week farmers voiced concern about forecasts of colder night temperatures but a British Sugar official said the crop was holding up well despite weekend frosts and had benefited from increased rainfall.
"The frost hasn't affected the crop," he said. Sugar beet needs a warm seed bed to germinate.
According to independent forecaster Weather Services Corp (WSC), Britain should see showers on Wednesday, followed by fair weather on Thursday and Friday.
It was expected to be warm on Wednesday but cooler again by Friday, WSC said.
Other beet sources said although there were still weeds, the rains had helped the crop get over its earlier problems with mice destroying seeds lying in dry beds

"It all seems to be improving with all the rain people have had. I don't think there are any problems at the moment...although there has been some re-drilling," said an official at the National Farmers Union (NFU).
"I think generally people are quite happy with what they've got," she said.
Farming sources said patchy emergence could be a problem as bed conditions varied during drilling, which ended ahead of last year's programme.
But although the recent rains helped to balance out the different stages of development, the crop still needed more moisture.
"It's not enough but it's something at least to get those seeds which hadn't emerged to come out," the NFU official said. --Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
